The Canvas simulation in this directory is a port of [stackedlol/ascii-sharks](https://github.com/stackedlol/ascii-sharks), pinned to commit `a0074c16a106f0abc665fe9712ca445f8f98ad8e`. The simulation, species and world sources are unmodified.

The upstream project is distributed under the MIT License in `LICENSE`. Upstream only draws light on black. The author's suggested light-theme CSS filter (`invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg)`) was tried and rejected: the body shading spans levels 12–226, so inversion maps the whole shadow half of the ramp to pale tones close to white, and at real glyph weights the sharks read as washed-out fragments on a light background. The renderer therefore carries two deliberate deviations: a native light palette (`OceanColorScheme`, `LIGHT_DOT_RGB` / `LIGHT_WATER_STOPS` / `LIGHT_ACCENTS` and the light branches in `drawSharks`), driven by the app's single theme chain (`theme-init.js` → `effectiveTheme` → `OceanEngine.setColorScheme`); and a finer cell grid on large screens (`cw = clamp(round(width / 168), 8, 13)` instead of upstream's `/ 124`). Upstream's divisor targets small demo canvases: on a full-size login screen it leaves each shark only ~150 coarse cells, so bodies read as thin ribbons. The finer grid gives the same silhouettes ~250 cells and they read as complete sharks; geometry, species and simulation are untouched. Dark rendering is otherwise the upstream behaviour. The shark roster shown on the login page is configured in Personal Settings and stored with the shared appearance settings. Geist Mono 600 is self-hosted as an exact-glyph WOFF2 subset under the SIL Open Font License in `/fonts/geist-mono-OFL.txt`.
